items.title: Foreigner nabbed for breaking auxiliary cop's teeth, damaging Genting casino
items.summary: KUANTAN: A foreigner was arrested for allegedly injuring an auxiliary policeman and damaging casino equipment at Sky Casino in Genting Highlands yesterday. Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said preliminary investigations revealed that the 34-year-old man, believed to have been drunk, had behaved aggressively towards members of the public before entering the casino. Azmi said the man also allegedly punched a 32-year-old auxiliary policeman in the mouth, breaking two of his teeth.

items.title: [UPDATED] BN, PN ink pact to face 16th Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional and its strategic partner Pas, representing parties under Perikatan Nasional, today formalised their cooperation and political understanding ahead of the 16th Melaka election. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed this evening by him and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also Pas secretary-general. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi witnessed the signing.

items.title: No confirmation of Malaysians affected by Spain train collision, embassy contacts authorities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian embassy in Madrid has yet to receive confirmation of any Malaysians affected by a collision involving two high-speed passenger trains near Urda in Toledo, Spain. The Foreign Ministry said it was closely monitoring the situation through the embassy following the collision, which occurred at approximately 8.54am local time. "The embassy is in contact with the relevant Spanish authorities and railway operators to ascertain whether any Malaysians were among the passengers involved and to coordinate consular assistance should the need arise," the ministry said in a media advisory.

items.title: Cops detain three, seize 376.2kg of pangolin scales in Negri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized 376.2kg of pangolin scales worth an estimated RM376,200 in an integrated operation at a premises in Negri Sembilan yesterday. In a statement today, division commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said police found 15 boxes of pangolin scales during a search of the premises. Zaki said the case was being investigated under Section 68 of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), relating to offences involving wildlife, its parts or derivatives.

items.title: A-GC: Financial crime investigation reports presented to cabinet before public disclosure
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Reports arising from investigations by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) Special Investigation Committee on Financial Crime Issues will be presented to the cabinet for consideration and action before being made public. In a statement today, the A-GC said the committee had been mandated to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the trail of financial crimes from their earliest stages. The A-GC said investigations would involve cooperation among the relevant enforcement agencies to ensure coordinated and integrated action.

items.title: Buried alive: Baby in critical condition in Kapit
items.summary: KAPIT: A newborn baby boy was found buried alive near a rented house in Jalan Airport, here, yesterday. District police chief Deputy Superintendent Rohana Nanu said the baby was found by policemen who heard its while conducting a search in the area about 2.30pm. The newborn was found buried," she said when contacted today.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 28, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Officer jailed seven years A senior police officer was jailed seven years and six months for causing the death of student Muhammad Zaharif Affendi in 2023. Shuhaily status referred The police have referred Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain's service status at the border agency to the Attorney-General's Chambers for advice. Chegubard jailed four months Badrul Hisham Shaharin, or Chegubard, was jailed four months for criminal defamation involving the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

items.title: Heavy rain causes fallen trees, flash floods in several areas [WATCH]
items.summary: A tree fell along the Kerinchi Link Expressway, on the stretch from Bangsar towards Bukit Damansara, at about 5.10pm. "Fallen tree along the Kerinchi Link Expressway heading from Bangsar towards Bukit Damansara," he wrote. View on Threads "Safe ride everyone."

items.title: Oriental interest terminates proposed acquisition of Chin Hin Jitra and CHJ Motor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Property developer Oriental Interest Bhd will not proceed with the proposed RM280 million acquisition of the entire equity interest in Chin Hin (Jitra) Sdn Bhd and CHJ Motor Holdings Sdn Bhd. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Oriental Interest said the company and the vendor, LLSB 1980 Holdings Sdn Bhd, had mutually agreed to terminate, revoke and rescind the conditional share sale and purchase agreement through a termination agreement dated Oct 28, 2026. "Among other factors, the company took into consideration the longer than anticipated timeframe and additional resources required to fulfil the relevant regulatory, approval and procedural requirements for completion," said Oriental Interest.

items.title: Lawyers want restraint in disciplinary action against Shuhaily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The authorities should exercise restraint before making any decision on Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain's tenure as Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general. Shuhaily's lawyer, Datuk Baljit Singh Sidhu, said the charge against his client under Section 323 of the Penal Code should be considered in its proper legal context, stressing that the principle of innocent until proven guilty must remain paramount. Baljit also said public sentiment had been overwhelmingly supportive of the work Shuhaily had undertaken so far.

items.title: PHB acquires RM300mil logistics property in Penang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) has acquired a logistics property in Bayan Lepas Waterfront, Penang, from Titijaya Land Bhd for RM300 million as part of its strategy to expand its logistics portfolio and strengthen recurring income streams. The logistics commercial complex is fully leased to DHL Properties (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, providing PHB with a stable rental income stream. With this acquisition, PHB said the logistics segment now accounts for about 11 per cent of its total investment property portfolio, reflecting the company's growing focus on logistics and industrial assets.

items.title: Appeal court imposes 20-year sentence on headmaster for child sex offences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today sentenced a headmaster to 20 years in jail and 11 strokes of the cane for making pornography and committing physical sexual assault against a standard six student five years ago. A three-judge panel, chaired by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin alongside Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dismissed Anuar Kintan’s appeal against his conviction and sentence of nine years and eight strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court for the charge of making pornography. The court subsequently convicted him of the charge, sentencing him to 11 years with three strokes of the cane.

items.title: PM says Budget 2027 reinforces Islam, criticises ‘hypocrite’ accusation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that Budget 2027 was formulated to continue promoting Islam, including through specific measures to strengthen pondok religious schools nationwide. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government had sought the views of Islamic scholars and religious teachers in drawing up the budget to ensure that the development needs of Islam received due attention. Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan; and Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.

items.title: Ex-Axis Incorporation adviser loses appeal over false financial statements
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has dismissed an appeal by Lee Koon Huat, a former adviser to Axis Incorporation Bhd's board of directors, and upheld his conviction and sentence for offences involving the submission of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia. High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin ruled that the prosecution had proven the charges against Lee beyond reasonable doubt. The High Court also agreed with the SC's submission that the sentence was appropriate given Lee's role in the offences.

items.title: High Court dismisses ex-Axis adviser’s appeal, upholds jail term and RM800,000 fine
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The High Court here today dismissed the appeal by former Axis Incorporation Bhd board adviser Lee Koon Huat against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abetting the furnishing of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia. “The High Court further agreed with the SC’s submission that the sentence imposed against Lee was appropriate in view of Lee’s role in the commission of the offences. “As such, the court dismissed Lee’s appeal against sentence and upheld the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court, being six months’ imprisonment and a fine of RM200,000 for each charge or in default, six months’ imprisonment,” it said.

items.title: Anwar: Dialogue with Myanmar offers best hope for Rohingya solution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia has opted for diplomacy in dealing with the refugee issue involving Myanmar, despite facing international criticism over the government’s approach to resolving the matter, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the approach was necessary to seek a solution after years of criticism and condemnation directed at Myanmar had failed to bring about any significant change in the country’s policies. “When I invited Myanmar President (Min Aung Hlaing), what was the objective?

items.title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Families facing 6-9 months' wait for death certification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal would need to wait at least six to nine months for letters of presumed death, despite Nepal cutting the waiting period from 12 years to 45 days. Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH)'s spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said the letters were needed for families to obtain death certificates and access their missing relatives' assets to settle outstanding liabilities. Manivannan said Nepal had initially said the ordinance only needed cabinet approval, but now it must also be passed by its Parliament and gazetted.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia must embrace AI, quantum technology without losing cultural roots
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia must continue to master emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing, to remain competitive globally while preserving its religious and cultural identity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said technological advancement was essential to ensuring the country kept pace with global developments, but must be anchored in religious faith, moral values, culture and literature. Our faith, morals, values, culture and literature,” he said.

items.title: Man dies after being trapped in paper mill machine in Bentong
items.summary: Bentong acting district police chief DSP Azmi Mahmod said police received a call through the MERS 999 emergency system at 11.56pm, following which a team from the Bentong District Criminal Investigation Division and Karak Police Station was dispatched to the scene. "Preliminary investigations found no criminal element. The statement also said that all personnel at the Bentong District Police Headquarters extended their condolences to the victim's family.

items.title: Toddlers tied up with rags: 11 daycare workers jailed in Indonesia
items.summary: YOGYAKARTA: An Indonesian court sentenced 11 childcare workers on Wednesday to up to three years in prison for abusing toddlers at a daycare centre in a case that sparked nationwide outrage. Some of the children's mothers wiped away tears as Judge Sunaryanto handed down each sentence, ranging from two to three years, at a court in Yogyakarta on Java island. Police later said they had found 20 children crammed into a room just three metres long by three metres wide.

items.title: 'Eat the rich': Thousands protest graft, wildfires in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA: Thousands of Indonesians protested in Jakarta and other cities Wednesday against economic hardship, graft and the government's handling of devastating wildfires emitting a toxic haze that has sickened thousands. Many placards expressed anger towards President Prabowo Subianto, whose popularity two years into his term has reached record lows amid claims of widespread government corruption and growing authoritarianism. Nobody paid us.

items.title: Foreign e-commerce platforms to face e-invoicing, must open local offices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance Ministry will impose e-invoicing on foreign e-commerce platforms and their vendors, which will have to open offices in Malaysia. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Seri Armizan Mohd Ali said the Finance Ministry would implement the measure soon as an immediate step to monitor foreign platforms. "The Finance Ministry will also soon impose e-invoicing on these foreign platforms and their related vendors.

items.title: Saifuddin: More stringent checks at KLIA to combat drug smuggling
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — More stringent inspections are set to be implemented at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) following an increase in reported drug smuggling cases at the nation’s primary gateway, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry will also be identifying ‘blind spot’ areas that are not monitored by close circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the KLIA 1 and 2 terminals. He said both KLIA 1 and 2 have 5,000 operational CCTV cameras, but said there are still ‘blind spot’ areas.

items.title: Sinkhole appears in Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 2.5m-wide, 4m-deep sinkhole opened on Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir this afternoon, forcing a road closure and emergency repair works. Zairil said based on a report by the Public Works Department (PWD), the sinkhole was detected about 2pm near an open field at Lorong Mayang Pasir 4. "The affected stretch has been closed to traffic, with motorists advised to use Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1 as alternative routes.

items.title: TikTok accounts for 81pc of 47,412 cyberbullying posts flagged by MCMC
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Facebook accounted for the second-largest share, at 12 per cent, Bernama reported. Meanwhile, Fahmi said MCMC was examining the misuse of messaging applications such as WhatsApp and Telegram, particularly their end-to-end encryption features, which allow private groups to operate beyond public view. Fahmi said the review also covered the misuse of messaging platforms to sell prohibited goods, including drugs.

items.title: Anwar decries tendency to label others 'murtad', 'munafik'
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised certain people for readily labelling others as murtad (apostates) and munafik (hypocrites) despite having only limited religious knowledge. The prime minister said the tendency to judge others based solely on limited religious knowledge reflected a deeper problem, namely a failure to develop a sound understanding of Islam and put its values into practice in daily life. He said the tradition of scholarship and enlightenment must be strengthened to ensure that religious discussions do not spark tensions, but instead foster greater understanding among the public.

items.title: Maxis neither denies nor confirms merger report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd neither denied nor confirmed a media report of a merger today but acknowledged that it is always evaluating strategic opportunities and partnerships that are value accretive. The telecommunications company said this in response to Bloomberg's news report today on a possible merger with U Mobile Sdn Bhd. According to its website, Maxis currently has a market capitalisation of US$6.7 billion to US$6.9 billion (RM27.2 billion to RM28.3 billion) as of October 2026.

items.title: CTOS still assessing impact of cybersecurity incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd is continuing to assess the operational and financial implications of its previously disclosed cybersecurity incident as it strengthens measures to protect personal and customer data. CTOS' net profit rose 11.5 per cent to RM27.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.69 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 5.5 per cent to RM87.56 million year-on-year. For the first nine months, net profit increased 14 per cent to RM68.71 million from RM60.29 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 7.5 per cent to RM256.02 million from RM238.08 million.

items.title: CTOS Q3 net profit rises 11.5pct to RM27.54mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd's net profit rose 11.5 per cent to RM27.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.69 million a year earlier, supported by higher revenue. Revenue for the quarter increased 5.5 per cent to RM87.56 million from RM83.01 million in the corresponding period, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia. International revenue slipped 1.7 per cent to RM13.9 million from RM14.1 million, reflecting slower sales growth.

items.title: PG Doraisamy emerges as substantial shareholder in Kumpulan Jetson
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PG Doraisamy P Gopal, who was involved in an earlier attempt to overhaul Kumpulan Jetson Bhd's board of directors, has emerged as a substantial shareholder of the company with a 5.13 per cent direct stake. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Kumpulan Jetson said Doraisamy held 23.53 million shares following the acquisition of 553,700 shares through an open-market transaction on Oct 26. The group also included Yudishthiran Doraisamy, Dhayalini PG Doraisamy, Wong Hong Yuk and Teoh Cheng Fang.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 28, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed higher as improving external sentiment provided support to the market. The key index rose two points to close at 1,613. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM331,911.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia opts for diplomacy to address Myanmar refugee issue
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has opted for a diplomatic approach with Myanmar to address the issue of refugees from the country living in Malaysia, despite international criticism of the government's handling of the crisis, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said Malaysia's efforts to establish diplomatic ties with Myanmar did not mean it agreed with or endorsed the country's treatment of the Rohingya ethnic minority, but rather served as a channel to secure cooperation in addressing the refugee issue. "So, I think the way forward is to try to establish diplomatic relations with Myanmar.

items.title: At least 30 killed as two high-speed trains collide in Spain
items.summary: MADRID: At least 30 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said. Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train with at least one carriage remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line. Castilla-la Mancha regional government said the death toll had risen to 30 from 10 after earlier warning it could rise.

items.title: Father's lessons in resilience paved way for Nurhidayah's success [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A resilient spirit instilled in her from childhood helped Superintendent Nurhidayah Damanhoori prove that women can lead the police mounted unit, a role demanding physical endurance, specialised skills and discipline. She made history in 2018 as the first woman appointed commanding officer of the unit since its establishment in 1984. She said her late father, Damanhoori Salikin, played a pivotal role in shaping her physical and mental resilience from an early age.

items.title: Netanyahu survives election setback as Israeli Jews deliver clear backing
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Benjamin Netanyahu won the support of an unexpectedly clear majority of Israeli Jews in an election billed as a major turning point in his nation's history, apparently ensuring he will survive as prime minister at least in a caretaker role. With around 70.7 per cent of votes tallied on Wednesday morning, Israeli media forecast Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties winning 54 seats in parliament, far surpassing 47 for the opposition bloc of rival Gadi Eisenkot. Parties representing Israelis of Arab descent would win 19.

items.title: Malaysia to deploy latest body scanners at RTS Link border checkpoint
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Latest technology scanners will be deployed at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Bukit Chagar here once the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link starts operations early next year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the implementation of this technology marks a first for Malaysia and serves as part of efforts to enhance security at the nation’s entry points. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail (left) presenting a memento to his Singapore counterpart Sim Ann, who is the Second Minister for Home Affairs, at the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (FTX 2026) closing ceremony at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site Johor Bahru today, Oct 28, 2026.

items.title: Ex-convicts among nine arrested in Miri grave desecration probe
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Police have arrested nine men believed to be involved in grave desecration activities in the Miri district during a special operation from October 11 to 17. Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said investigations revealed that three of the suspects had prior criminal records. "Following our action and investigations, police have solved 15 reported grave desecration cases in the Miri district.

items.title: Man remanded over Facebook caricature allegedly insulting police
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 — Police have arrested a 50-year-old local man in connection with an investigation into a caricature allegedly insulting the police that went viral on social media. In a statement today, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the 50-year-old self-employed man was detained outside Menara Seri Wilayah P2a in Putrajaya yesterday. Adzli said police had seized a mobile phone believed to have been used to make the post.

items.title: What if a fire breaks out on the RTS Link? Malaysia and Singapore put their rescue plans to the test
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Malaysia and Singapore have demonstrated their ability to jointly manage cross-border emergencies involving the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, following a field exercise simulating a fire aboard a stranded train. Singapore’s Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann said the exercise, held yesterday, demonstrated effective coordination between agencies from both countries in responding swiftly and professionally to a simulated emergency. She said three key outcomes stood out during the exercise, namely real-time communication, coordinated deployment of emergency personnel, and effective command and control.

items.title: Ex-Selangau MP Baru Bian fails to throw out PKR’s RM10m lawsuit over party exit
items.summary: The court ordered the former Selangau Member of Parliament to pay RM4,000 in costs to PKR. Baru is among 16 former Members of Parliament and state assemblymen sued by PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh on behalf of the party for allegedly breaching the terms of a RM10 million bond they signed with the party. Also named as defendants are Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar, Datuk Mansor Othman, Datuk Mohd Rashid Hasnon, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and Datuk Seri R. Santhara Kumar.

items.title: GPS to contest all 82 seats in Sarawak election, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will contest all 82 state seats in Sarawak’s 13th state election. Sarawak Premier and GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the decision was reached following a meeting with the presidents of the coalition’s component parties today. GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.

items.title: Motorcyclist killed in Klang after collision with 4WD sends him into trailer’s path
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — A motorcyclist was killed after being run over by a trailer following a collision with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle travelling in the emergency lane along Jalan Pintasan Pelabuhan Barat, Klang, near here at 9am today. Klang Selatan police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the 37-year-old local man was pronounced dead at the scene due to severe injuries. The impact caused him to fall into the right lane, where he was run over by a trailer travelling in the adjacent lane.

items.title: All approved school projects will be completed, Fadhlina pledges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government has given its assurance that all approved school development projects will be implemented and completed, while projects that had to be cancelled due to specific factors will be resubmitted for fresh approval. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said issues such as land constraints and rising costs would not result in school development needs being neglected, adding that affected projects would be resubmitted to address the needs of the schools concerned. She said 131 new school construction and replacement projects, costing more than RM14.789 billion in total, had been approved between 2023 and 2027.

items.title: Klang art studio loses nearly RM2,000 in pre-dawn break-in, three nabbed
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — An art studio owner lost nearly RM2,000 after the studio in Bandar Bukit Tinggi, Klang was believed to have been broken into by three men on October 24. The South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said that in the incident around 4.20am, three suspects were believed to have prised open the grille door and wooden door of the premises before stealing the complainant’s belongings. “Acting on information, the police arrested three men aged between 22 and 30 years on October 27.

items.title: Govt plans national drought response as El Niño threatens extreme heat in early 2027, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) will propose the development of a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council to strengthen preparedness for the phenomenon. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposal would be submitted for the council’s consideration, so that action plans for floods and droughts could also be developed, in addition to the existing National Haze Action Plan. “This is something that will be brought to the National Disaster Management Council, so that, apart from an action plan for haze, we will also have action plans for floods and droughts,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds Perak businessman’s acquittal on 122 cheating, forgery charges in RM6m case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the acquittal of a businessman on 122 counts of cheating and using forged documents involving medical equipment supply investments worth more than RM6 million in 2015. A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and K. Muniandy dismissed the prosecution’s final appeal against the acquittal of N. Narendran, 46, by the Ipoh High Court in January 2022. On the contrary, the High Court correctly identified fatal fundamental flaws in the prosecution’s case, rendering the Sessions Court’s conviction unsafe to uphold,” he said.

items.title: The Selangor royal aide who wasn’t: Man nabbed over RM1.42m car and property scam
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 40-year-old suspect was arrested in Johor Bahru at about 5 pm yesterday following continuous intelligence gathering into 26 police reports received nationwide since 2023. He said investigations also found that the self-employed suspect had no affiliation with or official appointment at any palace or the Selangor royal institution. “In Selangor alone, 15 police reports have been lodged, involving losses amounting to RM960,020.

items.title: Severe storm alert: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain across KL, Selangor and eight states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states and federal territories, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds until 8pm today. In Selangor, the affected districts comprise Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling, and Hulu Selangor. Other peninsular locations on alert include Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Muallim), Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, and Raub), Negeri Sembilan (Seremban, Rembau, Port Dickson, and Jelebu), and Johor (Batu Pahat, Kluang, Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru, Pontian, and Kulai).

items.title: Fewer foreign workers, more jobs for Malaysians: DPM Zahid outlines government’s priorities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government will continue implementing measures to gradually reduce the country’s reliance on foreign workers, in line with the direction set out in the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. In a Facebook post today, Ahmad Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the efforts would take into account the actual needs of industries while prioritising employment opportunities for Malaysians. Ahmad Zahid said he had highlighted the matter while chairing the third Cabinet Committee Meeting on Foreign Workers at Parliament today.

items.title: MACC monitoring over, but HRD Corp must now show results from RM2b training levies, says MEF
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called on the Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) to prioritise skills development, training quality and measurable workplace outcomes following the conclusion of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) governance monitoring of the agency. MEF Senior Advisor for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the conclusion of the monitoring marked an important step towards restoring employers’ confidence in HRD Corp following the implementation of governance improvement measures. “The conclusion of MACC’s governance monitoring is a positive development.

items.title: Who’s behind the haze? No conclusive evidence linking Malaysian firms to Indonesia fires, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — There is no conclusive evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said. He said NRES and the Plantation and Commodities Ministry had examined allegations that Malaysian companies were involved in burning activities in Indonesia. Arthur said the proposal to restrict financing for companies proven to be responsible for haze pollution required further scrutiny, particularly regarding the legal basis, evidentiary standards, jurisdiction and implications for the financial sector.

items.title: ‘All is well, kita Geng Biru’: Zahid signals unity after meeting MCA’s Wee Ka Siong amid Melaka seat row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir met MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong at the Parliament building today, believed to be over seat allocation ahead of the Melaka state election. The three leaders were seen entering the Members of Parliament Block at about 12.20pm amid a dispute over the announcement of BN candidates for the polls. MCA leaders are also understood to be scheduled to hold a meeting at Wisma MCA this afternoon following the meeting.

items.title: Botched Pahang raid leaves member of public injured, National Anti-Drugs Agency considers body cameras for officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) will discuss with the Home Ministry (KDN) a proposal to seek funding from the Finance Ministry for the procurement of body cameras for its enforcement officers. Its director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move followed a recommendation by the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) for KDN to prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK officers conducting field operations. Yesterday, the EAIC recommended that KDN prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK enforcement personnel following an incident during an operation to locate a suspected individual in Bera last year.

items.title: Family apologises to Bella Astillah over Muar woman’s viral grab-and-kiss incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The family of a wedding guest who went viral for grabbing Bella Astillah by the back of her neck to kiss her on the cheek has publicly apologised to the singer-actress. The woman’s daughter-in-law phoned in to ERA radio station’s 3 Pagi ERA segment to tender the apology after previous attempts to reach Bella through Instagram direct messages went unanswered, Berita Harian reported. “Our whole family tried sending Bella direct messages on Instagram, but there was no response.

items.title: KLIA Customs seizes RM49.5m in AI chips with potential military uses, fifth case in RM100m syndicate probe
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) foiled an attempt to transit 30 servers containing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth nearly RM49.5 million without the required authorisation. items.title: Behind Chow Kit shopfronts, Immigration uncovers alleged illegal money transfer network, eight detained
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — An illegal money transfer syndicate using the ‘Hundi’ system and targeting Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley was uncovered after the Immigration Department raided three premises in Chow Kit yesterday, where the activities were being conducted under the guise of retail and wholesale businesses. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the special operation, which began at 2.37pm, led to the arrest of eight Bangladeshi men aged between 24 and 42 following a month of intelligence gathering. “The syndicate is believed to have targeted Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley by using e-wallet accounts and local bank accounts registered under the names of foreign agents to conduct financial transactions.

items.title: KLIA Customs seizes RM1m in cannabis and ketamine hidden in shoes, toys and tool shipments
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has foiled two attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers and ketamine weighing a total of 16.39kg and worth RM1.03 million. KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag. Tuah said the first case involved the seizure of seven packages containing 7.28kg of cannabis flowers worth RM582,400 at the Pos Malaysia International Mail Centre at KLIA on October 12.

items.title: Malaysia to introduce new rules on AI use in court within next few weeks, says Chief Justice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The judiciary will issue a new practice direction on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) by lawyers and court officers in legal proceedings within the next few weeks, says Chief Justice (CJ) Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh. He said the move came amid concerns over the reliability of AI-generated legal submissions, which could appear convincing despite containing inaccurate information. Wan Ahmad Farid stressed that while technology could help accelerate the administration of justice, it should never replace human judgment, particularly when courts are required to exercise judicial discretion.

items.title: RM1m to look the other way? Two enforcement officers among five nabbed in Johor MACC foreign worker graft probe
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — The Johor Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded five individuals, including two federal enforcement agency officers, on suspicion of soliciting and receiving about RM1 million in bribes from a foreign worker agency. Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid said a five-day remand order until November 1 was issued by Magistrate A. Dhilip Nair at the Johor Bahru Court Complex here today, after allowing an application by the commission. He said the other three individuals detained were foreign worker agents.
